correctness.rationale: Rank-one purity of every successful output forces each contributing product Kraus A⊗B to map the three-dimensional antisymmetric support into the target line. A nonzero contributing branch has rank A=rank B=2 with a common one-dimensional kernel; otherwise an antisymmetric input involving a kernel vector would map to a nonzero product vector in an entangled target line. On the common two-plane, writing X=A†A and Y=B†B gives |alpha|^2=(TrX TrY-Tr(XY))/2. The matrix equation for the antisymmetric vector and Schatten Hölder gives TrX TrY>=2|alpha|^2(c+s)^2, hence Tr(XY)>=2 sin(2theta)|alpha|^2. Summing success effects E and using that the separable failure effect R=I-E has nonnegative trace pairing with the swap F yields 3=TrF>=Tr(FE)>=2 sin(2theta) sum|alpha|^2. Since each branch succeeds on P_-/3 with probability |alpha|^2/3, p<=1/[2 sin(2theta)]. The six explicit ordered-pair product Kraus operators in RESULT.md attain p=min{1,1/[2 sin(2theta)]}; their summed effect is diagonal with coefficients at most one and the diagonal complement is a separable failure effect. Boundary theta=pi/4 gives 1/2 and sin(2theta)=1/2 joins the deterministic branch continuously.
